axes.title: Temperament: calm to hot-headed
axes.note: What a person is like by nature, not what they do to others.

axes.title: Provoking: soothing to enraging
axes.note: What you do to someone else's temper.

axes.title: Speech: condemning to praising
axes.note: Verbs and nouns for what you say about someone.

axes.title: Reputation: smearing to honouring
axes.note: Attacks on standing rather than on an argument.

axes.title: A piece of angry speech
axes.note: All nouns for hostile talk, differing mainly in length and heat.

axes.title: Length: terse to long-winded
axes.note: Style of expression. Taciturn and reticent describe the person, not the prose.

axes.title: Change: making better to making worse
axes.note: The two poles are ameliorate and exacerbate.

axes.title: Money: miserly to extravagant
axes.note: A single scale from hoarding through prudence to waste.

axes.title: Stage: just starting to fully formed
Feeling: restrained to overwrought
axes.note: How much feeling is shown, not how much is had.

axes.title: A short saying: sharp to worn out
Judgement: impartial to biased
axes.note: Disinterested means impartial, never bored. It is one of the most reliable GRE traps.

axes.title: Currency: outdated to of the moment
Response to a fault: pardon to retribution
Bearing: beside the point to central
